TOKENAMUN  what-if: cache-ttl

switch the prompt cache from the 5-minute TTL to the 1-hour TTL
Session carry-fixture, 8 API calls

Observed
  observed TTL                                 5m
  cache writes at 5m                                 74,900   [observed]
  cache writes at 1h                                      0   [observed]
  prompt cost                                       107,359   [observed]
  expiry calls, gap under an hour                         1   [observed]
  expiry calls, gap over an hour                          0   [observed]

Derived
  re-creation avoidable under a 1h TTL               34,500   [derived]
  re-creation still required                              0   [derived]
      gaps longer than an hour expire under either TTL

Counterfactual
  saved by avoided re-creation                      -39,675   [counterfactual]
  cost of remaining re-creation at 2.0x                   0   [counterfactual]
  ordinary writes repriced 1.25x to 2.0x             30,300   [counterfactual]
  net change                                         -9,374   [counterfactual]
      negative is a saving; a session of short bursts that never idles
      past five minutes comes out positive, which is the point of
      computing it
  net change, share of prompt cost                    -8.7%   [counterfactual]

Caveat
  A real setting, and it can cost more than it saves.
  promptCacheTtl, Claude Code v2.1.242+. Comes out positive on sessions of
  short bursts, where the doubled write price buys a lifetime you never
  use.

Unknown
  - behavioural_change: the agent's trajectory is assumed identical. It
    would not have been.
  - idle_gap_distribution: future sessions may pause differently.
  - other_bucket: subagent, workflow and compaction requests need
    subagentPromptCacheTtl set separately.
  - provider_support: 1-hour availability varies on Bedrock and through
    gateways.
  - task_success: not observable from this data. An agent that fails the
    task consumes the fewest tokens of all, so a reduction is not an
    improvement.
